schema.description: The JSON body that LoonFS APIs return with an HTTP error status.

details.description: Optional machine-readable context for the error code.

feature.description: The capability feature that isn't supported, when the code is `not_supported`.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.

param.description: The invalid input, as a JSON Pointer, a parameter name, a CLI flag, or a CLI argument.

request_id.description: The request ID. The server also sends this ID in the `x-request-id` response header.

UnavailableResponse.description: The server can't complete the request now. Check `code` to find whether the cause is a deadline, shutdown, load, writer session admission, required maintenance, or invalid storage credentials. When its request cap is full, the reference server returns `server_busy` with `Retry-After: 1` before it reads the body. Health and readiness probes are exempt from the cap. A mutation might still complete after a deadline or a lost acknowledgment, so check its outcome before retrying.

AbsolutePath.description: A complete absolute path in the namespace, validated and serialized as a plain string.

AccessGrants.description:
A map from each principal to its rights.

The map can have at most 1,000 entries and 65,536 bytes of principal IDs, and no entry has an
empty set of rights. Decoding rejects a repeated principal.

AccessRevisionNo.description: The number of one revision of an inode's access row. It increases with every accepted access update.

AccessRight.description: One right that a grant can include.

AccessRights.description:
A set of rights.

The set is encoded as distinct right names in `read`, `history`, `write`, `create`, `remove`,
`share`, `manage`, `admin` order. Decoding accepts any order and rejects a repeated name.

ActorId.description: A stable, opaque actor ID of 1 to 256 visible ASCII characters.

AttributeKey.description:
The validated name of an inode attribute, from 1 to 128 UTF-8 bytes without control
characters.

Keys are compared byte for byte. Writes reject the reserved `loonfs.` prefix, even though
the type accepts it.

AttributeValue.description:
One validated inode attribute value of at most 4,096 UTF-8 bytes.

Empty strings and control characters are valid, and an attribute is deleted only by an
explicit remove operation.

Attributes.description:
A map from attribute keys to values, with at most 100 entries and 65,536 UTF-8 bytes of keys and
values in total.

Construction and decoding reject a map over these limits. An empty map means that the inode has
no attributes.

AttributesRevisionNo.description: The number of one revision of an inode's attributes. It starts at 0 and increases with every accepted attribute update, even when the map doesn't change.

BindingVersion.description: An opaque token for one version of a parent and name binding.

CapabilityDocument.description: The API groups, features, and limits that a deployment advertises.

api_groups.description:
The advertised API groups, as `group/version`. The deployment implements every required
operation in each group.

features.description:
Feature keys, and whether this deployment supports each one. An absent key means the feature
isn't supported.

limits.description: Advisory numeric limits that clients can use to check requests before sending them.

ChangeSeq.description: The sequence number of one namespace commit. Commits become visible in the order of these numbers.

Checkpoint.description: One checkpoint, as its durable record stores it.

captured_seq.description: The namespace sequence that the checkpoint captured.

checkpoint_id.description: The checkpoint's durable ID. For a user pin, it's also the snapshot's `snapshot_id`.

created_at_ms.description: The time the checkpoint record was created, in Unix milliseconds.

expires_at_ms.description:
The time the checkpoint expires, in Unix milliseconds. Garbage collection waits one more
grace window before it deletes the record.

manifest_no.description: The manifest that the checkpoint pins.

namespace_id.description: The namespace that the checkpoint belongs to.

owner.description: The checkpoint's owner. For a user pin, the owner includes the label.

CheckpointOwner.description: The owner of a checkpoint record.

CheckpointOwnerFork.description: A pin that keeps the source state that one fork attempt starts from.

target_namespace_id.description:
The fork's target namespace. Garbage collection keeps this checkpoint while that
namespace exists.

CheckpointOwnerUser.description: A snapshot, which a caller created. It's deleted by its ID or after it expires.

name.description: The label that the creator recorded. Labels don't need to be unique.

Checksum.description: A checksum algorithm and the checksum's canonical lowercase hexadecimal value.

value.description: The checksum in canonical lowercase hexadecimal, without a prefix.

Commit.description: One commit, including its identity and the events it applied.

committed_at_ms.description:
The time the commit was made, in Unix milliseconds. Commit order comes from `committed_seq`,
not from this time.

committed_by.description: The actor responsible for the commit, as the application supplied it.

committed_seq.description: The sequence at which the commit became visible.

events.description: The semantic filesystem changes that the commit applied, in request order.

message.description: The caller's optional annotation for the commit.

namespace_id.description: The namespace that changed.

CommitId.description:
The client's idempotency key for one logical commit.

Reuse the same commit ID when you retry the same request. A commit ID is 1 to 128 lowercase
ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens, and it starts with a letter or digit.
Generated commit IDs have the form `c_` followed by 26 lowercase Crockford base 32
characters, but callers can supply any value that follows these rules.

CommitPrecondition.description:
A condition that a commit must meet before its operations run.

The server checks each condition against the state before the commit. When several commits are
applied as one batch, that state's head sequence is the sequence of the last commit admitted
earlier in the batch, or the batch's starting head sequence if no earlier commit was admitted.

CommitPreconditionAccessRevision.description: A requirement that the inode is visible and has the access revision that the caller read.

expected_access_revision_no.description: The access revision that the caller observed.

inode_id.description: The inode whose state the caller read.

CommitPreconditionAttributesRevision.description: A requirement that the inode is visible and has the attribute revision that the caller read.

expected_attributes_revision_no.description: The attribute revision that the caller observed.

inode_id.description: The inode whose state the caller read.

CommitPreconditionFileRevision.description: A requirement that the inode is visible and has the content revision that the caller read.

expected_revision_no.description: The content revision that the caller observed.

inode_id.description: The inode whose state the caller read.

CommitPreconditionInodeBinding.description: A requirement that a visible inode still has the binding that the caller read.

expected_binding_version.description: The binding version that the caller observed.

inode_id.description: The inode whose binding the caller read.

CommitPreconditionNameAbsence.description: A requirement that no visible entry with this name exists under the parent inode.

CommitPreconditionNamespaceHead.description: A requirement that the head sequence before the commit equals `expected_head_seq`.

expected_head_seq.description: The head sequence that the caller observed when it read its inputs.

CommitPreconditionPathAbsence.description: A requirement that no visible entry exists at the full path.

path.description: The absolute path to check, which can be the root.

CommitPreconditionPathBinding.description: A requirement that the path still has the binding that the caller read.

expected_binding_version.description:
The binding version that the path must also have, if set. This check detects an inode
that was moved away from the path and then back.

expected_inode_id.description: The inode that the path must be bound to.

path.description: The absolute path to check, which can be the root.

CommitRequest.description:
A request to commit one or more filesystem operations atomically, in order.

The server rejects unknown fields.

commit_id.description: The caller's idempotency key for the whole request.

content_tokens.description: One content token for each uploaded `content_ref` that the request uses.

message.description: An annotation from the caller. The message is part of the commit's identity.

operations.description: The operations to commit atomically, in order. The list can't be empty.

preconditions.description: The conditions that the server checks, in order, before it runs any operation.

CompleteUploadBody.description: A request to complete an upload, in the mode that started it.

CompleteUploadBodyDirectMultipart.description: The completion of a direct multipart upload.

content.description: The expected length and checksum of the assembled object.

parts.description: The uploaded parts, in ascending part order.

CompleteUploadBodyDirectPut.description: The completion of a direct PUT upload.

content.description: The expected length and checksum of the stored object.

CompleteUploadBodyServiceProxied.description: The completion of a service-proxied upload.

CompletedUploadPart.description: One uploaded part that the object store provider accepted.

checksum.description: The checksum that the part was signed and accepted with.

etag.description: The entity tag that the provider returned for the accepted part.

ContentId.description: The random identity of one immutable content object.

ContentRef.description: A reference to a prefix of one content chain, by its owner, content ID, size, and checksum.

checksum.description: The required checksum of the referenced bytes.

content_id.description:
The immutable identity of the content. The content ID and the owner together determine the
object key.

kind.description: The kind of content reference. The format defines one kind, `blob_v1`.

owner_namespace_id.description: The namespace that originally wrote the bytes.

size_bytes.description: The length of the referenced bytes, which are a prefix of the content object.

ContentRefKind.description: A supported kind of content reference, serialized as a string.

ContentToken.description:
A signed token that shows a `content_ref` was verified in a completed upload, so a later
commit can use that reference.

content_ref.description: The content that this token authorizes.

token.description: The opaque token that the server signed. Clients must not parse it.

CreateDownloadByInodeRequest.description: A request to download a file inode's current revision.

consistency.description:
How recently the read confirms the namespace head. `eventual` (the default, unless the
server's `consistency` setting is `strong`) reads at the head that the server confirmed last
while that confirmation is younger than the maximum staleness, and `strong` confirms the
head before the read. It can't be combined with `snapshot_id`.

max_staleness_ms.description:
With `consistency` set to `eventual`, how old the server's last confirmation of the head can
be, in milliseconds. The default is the server's `max_staleness_ms`.

snapshot_id.description:
A snapshot to read the file from. The download reads the revision that the snapshot
captured.

start_offset.description:
The first byte that the grant reads. It defaults to 0 and must be less than the file's size.
For a file of zero bytes, it must be 0.

CreateDownloadByInodeResponse.description: A short-lived capability to read one revision of an inode.

content_ref.description: The content's identity, size, and checksum.

inode_id.description: The file inode being read.

namespace_id.description: The namespace that was read.

ranges.description: The ranges that cover the revision's bytes from the requested offset, in order.

CreateDownloadRequest.description: A request to download a file by path, and optionally a revision.

consistency.description:
How recently the read confirms the namespace head. `eventual` (the default, unless the
server's `consistency` setting is `strong`) reads at the head that the server confirmed last
while that confirmation is younger than the maximum staleness, and `strong` confirms the
head before the read. It can't be combined with `snapshot_id`.

max_staleness_ms.description:
With `consistency` set to `eventual`, how old the server's last confirmation of the head can
be, in milliseconds. The default is the server's `max_staleness_ms`.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to read.

revision_no.description:
The revision to read. Omit it to read the path's current revision. It can't be combined with
`snapshot_id`.

snapshot_id.description:
A snapshot to read the file from. The download reads the revision that the snapshot
captured. It can't be combined with `revision_no`.

start_offset.description:
The first byte that the grant reads. The grant covers the revision's bytes from
`start_offset` up to `size_bytes`, so a client that resumes a download asks for a new grant
that starts after the bytes it already has. The offset must be less than the revision's
size. For a revision of zero bytes, it must be 0.

CreateDownloadResponse.description: The signed object ranges for one revision.

content_ref.description: The identity, byte length, and checksum of the revision's bytes.

namespace_id.description: The namespace that was read.

path.description: The absolute path, built from the stored display names.

ranges.description: The ranges that cover the revision's bytes from the requested offset, in order.

revision_no.description: The revision that the capability reads, as resolved from the request.

CreateNamespaceRequest.description: A request to create a namespace.

access.description:
The namespace's access mode, which can't be changed after the namespace is created. The
default is unrestricted.

namespace_id.description: The durable ID of the new namespace.

retention_window_ms.description:
The namespace's retention window, in milliseconds, which must be positive. The reference
server's maintenance sweep then uses this window for the namespace instead of the server's
`retention_window_ms` setting. A `retention_window` maintenance run can change or clear the
window later.

CreateRevisionDownloadByInodeRequest.description: A request to download one retained revision of an inode.

consistency.description:
How recently the read confirms the namespace head that it finds the revision in. `eventual`
(the default, unless the server's `consistency` setting is `strong`) reads at the head that
the server confirmed last while that confirmation is younger than the maximum staleness,
and `strong` confirms the head before the read.

max_staleness_ms.description:
With `consistency` set to `eventual`, how old the server's last confirmation of the head can
be, in milliseconds. The default is the server's `max_staleness_ms`.

start_offset.description:
The first byte that the grant reads. It defaults to 0 and must be less than the revision's
size. For a revision of zero bytes, it must be 0.

CreateSnapshotRequest.description: A request to create a snapshot.

name.description: The snapshot's label, which doesn't need to be unique.

ttl_ms.description:
The snapshot's lifetime in milliseconds, counted from the server's current time. Omit it to
keep the snapshot until it's deleted.

CreateUploadBody.description: The transport for a new upload session.

CreateUploadBodyDirectMultipart.description: A transport in which the client writes the object in parts through presigned part uploads.

part_size_bytes.description: The byte length of every part except the last. Omit it to use the server default.

CreateUploadBodyDirectPut.description: A transport in which the client writes the whole object through one presigned request.

size_bytes.description: An advisory byte length, which the server uses to check the provider's size limit early.

CreateUploadBodyServiceProxied.description:
A transport in which the client sends the bytes to the service, which writes the content
object.

DeleteDirectoryBehavior.description: Whether a delete can remove a non-empty directory.

DeleteNamespaceResponse.description: The result of deleting a namespace.

head_seq.description: The last committed sequence before the namespace was deleted.

namespace_id.description: The deleted namespace.

DeleteSnapshotResponse.description: The snapshot record that was deleted.

namespace_id.description: The namespace that the snapshot belonged to.

snapshot_id.description: The ID of the deleted snapshot record.

DeletedCheckpointsByOwner.description: The number of checkpoint records that one garbage collection pass deleted, grouped by owner.

fork.description: The fork pins that the pass deleted because their target namespaces no longer exist.

user.description: The user pins that the pass deleted after they expired or their namespace was deleted.

DeletedObjectCounts.description: The number of objects that one garbage collection pass deleted, grouped by object family.

content_objects.description:
The content objects the pass deleted because no retained view referenced them and they were
older than the grace window.

manifests.description: The unreferenced manifests that the pass deleted.

metadata_segments.description: The unreferenced metadata segments that the pass deleted.

retired_content_objects.description: The content objects that the pass listed under a retired namespace and deleted.

temporary_objects.description:
The store's temporary objects that the pass deleted because they were older than the grace
window.

upload_sessions.description: The upload session records that the pass deleted after their grace windows passed.

wal_objects.description: The unreferenced WAL objects that the pass deleted.

DestinationBehavior.description: What a path put, move, or copy does when the destination already exists.

DirectoryBinding.description: A directory entry's parent and name.

name_key.description: The name key that lookups use to find the entry.

parent_inode_id.description: The parent directory that contains the entry.

DisplayName.description: One path component, spelled as users see it.

DownloadRange.description: One contiguous run of a revision's bytes, which the client reads from one object.

access.description: A short-lived read capability for exactly this range's bytes.

length.description: The number of bytes in the run.

start_offset.description: The offset of the run's first byte in the revision.

ErrorDetails.description:
The machine-readable identifiers and state that explain an error response.

Every field is optional.

active_acquired_at_ms.description:
The time the current writer acquired its epoch, in Unix milliseconds. It's present when the
current manifest records a writer.

active_writer_id.description: The writer of the current epoch. It's present when the current manifest records a writer.

actual_access_revision_no.description: The access revision that is actually current for the inode.

actual_attributes_revision_no.description: The attribute revision that is actually current for the inode.

actual_deletion_seq.description: The deletion sequence that is actually active for the inode.

actual_inode_id.description: The inode that the path actually contained.

actual_revision_no.description: The revision that is actually current. It's absent when the inode has no current revision.

after_seq.description: The `after_seq` value from the change feed request.

commit_id.description: The idempotency key of the commit that the error is about.

committed_fingerprint.description:
The fingerprint of the mutation that was committed under `commit_id`. This field is present
exactly when `committed_seq` is present.

committed_seq.description:
The sequence that `commit_id` was already committed at. The server includes it when a
durable commit receipt records that commit.

expected_access_revision_no.description: The access revision that the request expected to be current.

expected_attributes_revision_no.description: The attribute revision that the request expected to be current.

expected_binding_version.description: The opaque binding token that the request supplied.

expected_deletion_seq.description: The deletion sequence that the undelete expected to be active.

expected_head_seq.description: The head sequence that the request required.

expected_inode_id.description: The inode that the request expected the path to contain.

expected_revision_no.description: The revision that the request expected to be current.

fenced_writer_epoch.description: The epoch of the failed writer session at the time another writer displaced it.

inode_id.description: The inode that the failed precondition or operation targeted.

namespace_id.description: The deleted namespace that caused the operation to fail.

operation_index.description: The index of the failed operation in the request.

precondition_index.description: The zero-based position of the failed request precondition.

retention_floor_seq.description:
The namespace's retention floor. A change feed request can set `after_seq` to this sequence
or any later one, and the feed returns the changes committed after it.

size_bytes.description:
For `range_not_satisfiable`, the size in bytes of the file that the range was requested
from.

ErrorResponse.description: The JSON body that LoonFS APIs return with an HTTP error status.

details.description: Optional machine-readable context for the error code.

feature.description: The capability feature that isn't supported, when the code is `not_supported`.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.

param.description: The invalid input, as a JSON Pointer, a parameter name, a CLI flag, or a CLI argument.

request_id.description: The request ID. The server also sends this ID in the `x-request-id` response header.

ExtendSnapshotRequest.description: A request to extend a snapshot.

ttl_ms.description: The new lifetime in milliseconds, counted from the server's current time.

ExtensionGcReports.description:
The reports from the extension collectors that one `gc` run ran, with one optional field for
each extension.

Each extension reports its collector under its own name here. A deployment that doesn't
maintain an extension's state leaves that extension's field out, and a client ignores a name
it doesn't know.

grep.description:
The counts from the grep index's collector, present when the deployment maintains a grep
index.

FileRevision.description: One immutable revision of a file.

commit_id.description: The ID of the commit that created this revision.

committed_at_ms.description:
The time the revision was committed, in Unix milliseconds. Commit order comes from
`committed_seq`, not from this time.

committed_by.description: The actor responsible for this revision, as the application supplied it.

committed_seq.description: The namespace sequence of the commit that created this revision.

content_ref.description: The content stored for this revision.

inode_id.description: The file inode that this revision belongs to.

revision_no.description: The revision number within the file inode.

FilesystemChange.description:
One filesystem change within a commit.

One request operation can produce several changes.

A newer server can return a change kind that isn't listed here. Clients should skip a change
whose kind they don't recognize.

FilesystemChangeAccessChanged.description:
An inode's access row was replaced.

`grants` is the complete direct grant map after the update.

access_revision_no.description: The access revision that the update published.

boundary.description: Whether the directory stops inheriting grants from its ancestors.

grants.description: Every direct grant that the inode has after this update.

inode_id.description: The inode whose access row changed.

attributes.description:
The inode's complete attribute map after the update. The map is empty when the update
removed every attribute.

inode_id.description: The inode whose attributes changed.

FilesystemChangeContentChanged.description:
A file received a new current revision from a put, a copy, an append, or a revision
restore.

append_offset.description:
The offset where the appended bytes begin, present when an append published the
revision.

It equals the base revision's `size_bytes`, so the new revision's bytes are the base
revision's bytes followed by the bytes from this offset to `size_bytes`. It's
present for every append, including one that starts a new content ID, and absent for
a put, a copy, or a revision restore.

content_ref.description: The immutable content that the revision published.

inode_id.description: The file inode whose history advanced.

revision_no.description:
The file's new revision number, which is higher than the number of every earlier
revision.

FilesystemChangeDeleted.description: A file or directory subtree was deleted.

deleted_binding.description: The directory binding that the deletion removed.

inode_id.description: The inode at the root of the deleted subtree.

binding_version.description: The binding that this event created. The value is opaque.

display_name.description: The display name of the new entry.

inode_id.description: The newly allocated inode, unique within the namespace.

parent_inode_id.description: The directory that the new entry was bound under.

FilesystemChangeFileCreated.description: A file and its first revision were created.

binding_version.description: The binding that this event created. The value is opaque.

content_ref.description: The content of the first revision.

display_name.description: The display name of the new entry.

inode_id.description: The newly allocated inode, unique within the namespace.

parent_inode_id.description: The directory that the new entry was bound under.

FilesystemChangeMoved.description: An inode moved to a new parent directory or name.

binding_version.description: The binding that this event created. The value is opaque.

destination_display_name.description: The display name of the new binding.

destination_parent_inode_id.description: The directory that contains the new binding.

inode_id.description: The inode whose binding changed.

source_display_name.description: The display name of the removed binding.

source_parent_inode_id.description: The directory that contained the removed binding.

FilesystemChangeUndeleted.description: A deleted inode was recovered and re-bound.

binding_version.description: The binding that this event created. The value is opaque.

display_name.description: The display name of the recovered binding.

inode_id.description: The recovered inode.

parent_inode_id.description: The directory that the recovered entry was bound under.

FilesystemOperation.description:
One filesystem operation.

The server rejects unknown fields, and a variant without fields requires an empty object.

FilesystemOperationAppendFile.description: An operation that adds bytes to the end of a file as its next revision.

expected_inode_id.description: The inode that the path must still resolve to.

expected_revision_no.description: The content revision that must still be current. It requires `expected_inode_id`.

inline_content.description: The bytes to add, as base64, from 1 byte to 256 KiB.

path.description: The absolute path, which must resolve to a visible file.

FilesystemOperationAppendFileByInode.description: An operation that adds bytes to the end of a file inode as its next revision.

expected_revision_no.description: The content revision that must still be current.

inline_content.description: The bytes to add, as base64, from 1 byte to 256 KiB.

inode_id.description: The file to append to.

FilesystemOperationCopyByInode.description: An operation that copies a file inode to a new name under a parent inode.

behavior.description: Whether the operation can replace an existing destination file.

expected_destination_inode_id.description: The inode that the destination path must contain. It applies only with `replace` behavior.

expected_destination_revision_no.description:
The content revision that must be the destination file's current revision. It applies only
with `replace` behavior and requires `expected_destination_inode_id`.

inode_id.description: The file to copy.

FilesystemOperationCopyPath.description: An operation that copies a file from one path to another.

behavior.description: Whether the operation can replace an existing destination file.

destination_path.description: The absolute destination path. The destination's parent must be visible and writable.

expected_destination_inode_id.description: The inode that the destination path must contain. It applies only with `replace` behavior.

expected_destination_revision_no.description:
The content revision that must be the destination file's current revision. It applies only
with `replace` behavior and requires `expected_destination_inode_id`.

source_path.description: The absolute source path, which must resolve to a visible file.

FilesystemOperationCreateDirectory.description: An operation that creates one directory.

parents.description:
Whether the operation creates any missing ancestor directories. The final path component
must still be new.

path.description:
The absolute path of the new directory. The operation fails if the path is invalid or
already bound.

FilesystemOperationCreateDirectoryByInod.description: An operation that creates a directory under an existing parent inode.

display_name.description: The name of the new directory.

FilesystemOperationCreateFileByInode.description:
An operation that creates a file with an unused name under an existing parent inode.

The operation requires exactly one of `content_ref` and `inline_content`.

content_ref.description:
The uploaded content, which a content token must cover. Set this field or
`inline_content`, but not both.

display_name.description: The name of the new file.

inline_content.description: The complete file bytes as base64. Set this field or `content_ref`, but not both.

FilesystemOperationDeleteByInode.description:
An operation that deletes an inode if its current binding version is
`expected_binding_version`.

behavior.description: Whether the operation can recursively delete a non-empty directory.

expected_binding_version.description: The binding version that the inode must currently have for the delete to succeed.

inode_id.description: The inode to delete.

FilesystemOperationDeletePath.description: An operation that deletes the file or directory at one path.

behavior.description: Whether the operation can recursively delete a non-empty directory.

expected_inode_id.description: The inode that the path must still resolve to before the delete.

path.description: The absolute path, which must resolve to a visible inode.

FilesystemOperationMoveByInode.description:
An operation that moves an inode if its current binding version is
`expected_binding_version`.

behavior.description: Whether the operation can replace an existing destination file.

expected_binding_version.description: The binding version that the inode must currently have for the move to succeed.

expected_destination_inode_id.description: The inode that the destination path must contain. It applies only with `replace` behavior.

expected_destination_revision_no.description:
The content revision that must be the destination file's current revision. It applies only
with `replace` behavior and requires `expected_destination_inode_id`.

inode_id.description: The inode to move.

FilesystemOperationMovePath.description: An operation that moves a file or directory from one path to another.

behavior.description: Whether the operation can replace an existing destination file.

destination_path.description: The absolute destination path. The destination's parent must be visible and writable.

expected_destination_inode_id.description: The inode that the destination path must contain. It applies only with `replace` behavior.

expected_destination_revision_no.description:
The content revision that must be the destination file's current revision. It applies only
with `replace` behavior and requires `expected_destination_inode_id`.

source_path.description: The absolute source path, which must resolve to a visible inode.

FilesystemOperationPutFile.description:
An operation that creates or replaces one file from uploaded or inline content.

The operation requires exactly one of `content_ref` and `inline_content`.

behavior.description: Whether the operation adds a new revision to an existing file or fails with a conflict.

content_ref.description:
The uploaded content, which a content token must cover. Set this field or
`inline_content`, but not both.

expected_inode_id.description: The inode that the path must contain. It applies only with `replace` behavior.

expected_revision_no.description:
The content revision that must be the file's current revision. It applies only with
`replace` behavior and requires `expected_inode_id`.

inline_content.description: The complete file bytes as base64. Set this field or `content_ref`, but not both.

path.description: The absolute destination path. The operation creates any missing ancestor directories.

FilesystemOperationPutFileRevisionByInod.description:
An operation that adds a revision to a file inode if the inode's current revision is
`expected_revision_no`.

The operation requires exactly one of `content_ref` and `inline_content`.

content_ref.description:
The uploaded content, which a content token must cover. Set this field or
